paragraphs: Friend, this whole chapter is a list of jobs, and I think that's the point. Gatekeepers at the gates, treasurers over the treasuries, officers and judges over Israel. Every job in the house of the LORD gets a name and a place (1 Chronicles 26:12, 20, 29). Nobody in this passage is too small to be written down.

Now look at HOW the jobs get handed out. They cast lots for each gate, "young and old alike" (1 Chronicles 26:13). Nobody gets skipped because of age. And when the writer lists Obed-edom's eight sons, he says why: "For God had blessed Obed-edom" (1 Chronicles 26:5). I think that tells us the family, the strength and the work all came from the same hand.

And here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. Some of these men guard a gate, and some count gifts, and some handle "every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king" (1 Chronicles 26:32). Different posts, SAME house, SAME service. So whatever your post looks like today, whether it's loud or quiet or nobody-sees-it, it's part of the work of the LORD, and that's worth showing up for, friend.
